source_text: Legem Veteris Testamenti nos aiunt dicere non ob hoc datam fuisse, ut iustificaret oboedientes, sed ut gravioris fieret causa peccati
pass_a_gloss: They say that we say the Law of the Old Testament was not given for this, that it should justify those obeying, but that it should become a cause of heavier sin.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law

pass_b_english: They say that the law of the Old Testament was not given to justify those who obeyed it, but to become a cause of more serious sin.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian means Scripture's legal/authoritative witness, especially the divine Law as teacher of justice.
rejected: natural law (unless the sentence is philosophical)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian and fellow bishops (Collective letter to Thessalonica, words preserved in Augustine, Contra duas epistolas Pelagianorum 2–4); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
